findings.summary: TokenManager is created independently in both sync-command.ts and repository-processor.ts from the same env vars
evidence: sync-command.ts:574-581 creates an identical tokenManager from the same env vars
sync-command.ts:343 calls resolveGitHubToken with its own tokenManager, then passes the result as options.token to the processor, which also has its own tokenManager inside AuthOptionsBuilder
findings.suggestion: Inject a single tokenManager from the CLI composition root into RepositoryProcessor rather than having both layers independently read env vars and create their own instances. The processor's constructor already accepts a components bag — add tokenManager there or pass it through the existing GitOpsFactory.

findings.summary: SyncWorkflow re-packs the same fields (workDir, dryRun, retries, token, executor, repoInfo) into 3 different options bags per call
evidence: BranchSetupOptions has: repoInfo, branchName, baseBranch, workDir, isDirectMode, dryRun, retries, token, gitOps, executor (10 fields)
CommitPushOptions has: repoInfo, gitOps, workDir, fileChanges, commitMessage, pushBranch, isDirectMode, dryRun, retries, token, executor, hasAppCredentials (12 fields)
PRHandlerOptions has: branchName, baseBranch, workDir, dryRun, retries, prTemplate, token, executor (8 fields)
sync-workflow.ts:59-77 assembles BranchSetupOptions, then :96-109 assembles CommitPushOptions, then :140-154 assembles PRHandlerOptions — all pulling from the same local variables
findings.suggestion: Extract a shared 'RunContext' type containing the common fields (workDir, dryRun, retries, token, executor, repoInfo, gitOps) and have each options bag compose with it plus its unique fields, reducing re-assembly boilerplate in SyncWorkflow.

findings.summary: BranchManager and CommitPushManager call module-level factory functions (getPRStrategy, getCommitStrategy) instead of receiving strategies via DI
evidence: branch-manager.ts:34 calls getPRStrategy(repoInfo, executor, this.log) as a free function import
commit-push-manager.ts:49 calls getCommitStrategy(repoInfo, executor, options.hasAppCredentials) as a free function import
Both classes accept ILogger via constructor (DI pattern) but then use static factory calls for their main collaborators
findings.suggestion: Inject the strategy factories (or the strategies themselves) via constructor parameters to maintain consistent DI at integration seams. This also improves testability — currently tests must mock module-level imports rather than injecting test doubles.

findings.summary: Token resolution happens at two levels: sync-command resolves token then passes it down, but AuthOptionsBuilder can also resolve tokens independently
evidence: sync-command.ts:341-351 resolves token via resolveGitHubToken and passes as options.token
auth-options-builder.ts:25-27 short-circuits if preResolvedToken is provided, but lines 30-36 can also resolve independently
This creates two valid execution paths through the same seam — one where token is pre-resolved (sync-command path) and one where AuthOptionsBuilder resolves it (direct RepositoryProcessor usage)
findings.suggestion: Choose one canonical token resolution point. Either always resolve at the outer layer and remove the resolution capability from AuthOptionsBuilder, or always delegate to AuthOptionsBuilder and remove the sync-command resolution. Document the intended path clearly.

findings.summary: SyncWorkflow imports defaultExecutor singleton as fallback, breaking the DI pattern used elsewhere
evidence: sync-workflow.ts:43 uses it as fallback: const executor = options.executor ?? defaultExecutor
This is a library-layer module importing a global singleton, contrary to the CLAUDE.md rule: 'src/shared/ and src/sync/ modules must not import global singletons'
findings.suggestion: Make executor required in ProcessorOptions, or push the defaultExecutor fallback to the composition root (repository-processor.ts) where env access is expected.
